title: Response chunking vs full-frame: latency and cost brief (notes)
content:
Executive summary:

This note captures exploratory benchmarks comparing two response delivery strategies: streaming-by-chunk (incremental flushes of N tokens) vs full-frame delivery (buffer entire response then return). Goal: measure latency percentiles and token-level cost impact for different response lengths and chunk sizes, under sessionized and single-query loads.

Key takeaways (working):
- For long responses (>512 tokens), chunked streaming with chunk sizes between 256–512 tokens gives 30–55% perceived latency improvement (p50/p90) for the first bytes, with negligible increase in total GPU time for the majority of models we tested.
- Small chunk sizes (<=64) introduce measurable overhead due to repeated kernel dispatch and RPC chatter: p95 increased by ~10–25% and per-token compute cost rose by ~6–12% on A100 when session multiplexing is high.
- Full-frame still wins for short responses (<128 tokens) because it avoids streaming overhead and benefits from single contiguous kernel execution.
- For chat use-cases where UX value is front-loaded (first token matters), chunking is clearly preferred; for API use-cases that return short, precise outputs, full-frame produces slightly lower cost and simpler telemetry.

Measurement setup (abridged):
- Date: 2026-05-03 to 2026-05-06 (iterative runs)
- Code: local branch runtime/streaming-experiments, PR link above
- Hardware: A100-40GB (primary), T4 (spot-checks)
- Models: small-encoder-6B-quant (approx 6B INT8), base-34B-fp16 (approx 34B FP16), and rwd-tiny-1.3B (dev-only baseline)
- Workloads:
  - Single-query long-tail: prompt lengths at 64/128/256 with expected completions sampled at 128/256/512/1024 tokens
  - Sessionized interactive: synthetic sessions with 3–7 turns, median response 180 tokens, 95th 720 tokens
- Concurrency: low (10 qps), medium (80 qps), burst (300 qps sustained 30s)
- Metrics captured: first-byte latency (time to first chunk), p50/p90/p95 total-latency, tokens/sec (served), average GPU utilization, estimated $/1k tokens (back-of-napkin using instance-hour amortization)

Representative numeric table (p95 ms and relative $/1k tokens):

Scenario: base-34B-fp16 on A100, median prompt 128 tokens, target completion 512 tokens, medium concurrency (80 qps)

Strategy | chunk_size | first-byte p50 (ms) | total p95 (ms) | tokens/sec | est $/1k tokens
---------|------------|---------------------|----------------|------------|----------------
full-frame | - | 420 | 890 | 120 | $4.10
stream-512 | 512 | 180 | 920 | 118 | $4.15
stream-256 | 256 | 140 | 950 | 114 | $4.22
stream-128 | 128 | 120 | 1010 | 108 | $4.35
stream-64  | 64  | 110 | 1130 | 96  | $4.60

Notes on table: first-byte p50 gains are large for stream-512, stream-256. Total p95 slightly worse for streaming due to per-chunk scheduling tails in high-concurrency scenarios. $/1k tokens increases modestly as chunk size shrinks because overhead diffuses across more RPCs and kernel launches.

ASCII micro-chart: perceived latency curve (first-byte p50) vs chunk size for base-34B (lower is better)

chunk-size: 64    128   256   512   1024
first-byte(ms): 110  120   140   180   220
chart approx: 110 |***
           120 |****
           140 |******
           180 |**********
           220 |**************

Sessionized behavior (qualitative):
- When sessions reuse KV cache heavily, streaming introduces less incremental cost because the decoder path dominates; chunking overhead becomes amortized by faster first-byte delivery across turns.
- Cold sessions (no KV) magnify chunking overhead since each chunk touches host<->device transfers more frequently.

Edge cases observed:
- Microbursts (sudden 200–400 qps) cause chunked responses to have wider latency tails when the scheduler enqueues many small chunk continuations; in our burst-proof scheduler variant this was reduced but still present at p99.
- On T4 the gap between full-frame and chunked narrowed because kernel launch overhead is relatively higher; chunk sizes <=128 become expensive.

Developer/observability implications:
- Telemetry needs: track first-byte vs last-byte separately, and surface chunk_count per-response. Current dashboards only show total-latency which hides streaming benefits.
- Tracing: add chunk-id and chunk-schedule-latency events so we can attribute per-chunk stall sources (net vs runtime).
- Rollout strategy: enable stream-512 as default for interactive endpoints behind a feature flag. Expose client-side option for chunk size to accommodate edge devices.

Recommendations (short):
- Default: stream-256 for interactive chat endpoints with median response >200 tokens, fallback to full-frame for short-response routes.
- Expose: per-route streaming policy (auto/always/never) + auto-tune option that selects chunk size based on recent response-length distribution.
- Observability: add "first-byte latency" and "average chunk_size" to per-route dashboards; add an alert if chunk-count per response > 16 or if streaming increases token-cost by >10% over baseline.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Measure impact on token-accurate billing across real customer traces (need privacy-safe sample). Action: request CS anonymized trace dump for 5 top routes (JIRA-ENG-8842).
- Can we batch small-chunk RPCs at the transport layer to amortize network overhead? Prototype ticket in runtime backlog (PR linked).
- UX: measure subjective satisfaction vs first-byte latency improvements for real chat flows (small user study).

Quick TODOs:
- [ ] Run longer runs on T4 and older gen GPUs to build cost matrix (owner: Daniel)
- [ ] Hook chunk_count and first_byte to per-route SLIs (owner: Liu)
- [ ] Draft short doc for SDK teams with recommended defaults and flag usage (owner: Aisha)

Appendix (short methodology notes):
- Each datapoint is median over 5 runs of 2k requests each (where feasible); we warm cache for 3 iterations before measurement.
- Cost estimates are approximate: instance-hour amortization with GPU hourly cost assumptions (A100 $3.6/hr equivalent used). We do not include networking egress or storage.

References and links: see linked_artifacts above; also related internal notes: runtime/observability/streaming-telemetry-proto (internal confluence page to be created).

Note: draft-style notes; expect follow-up with formalized charts and heatmaps once we ingest customer trace sample.
